attrs.evidence: R5 needed a tenth kind, `cited_result`, because the flat list could not represent a KNOWN claim — and GPT-5.6's audit reads that correctly as a symptom rather than a fix. The list mixes axes: `counterexample` is logical force, `measurement` is acquisition mode, `cited_result` is origin, `reproduction` is corroboration, `attestation` is provenance assurance, `model_judgment` is source class. An externally published theorem that this tree independently reproduces from an attested artifact is simultaneously cited, deductive, reproduced and attested; the current schema makes it pick one. THE FAMILIAR PART is that this is the Periodic Table's own problem one level up — TAX-COMPOUND found that most classified cells need two or more kinds, and TAX-FLOW concluded the likelier resolution is orthogonal AXES rather than a yes/no on a ninth kind. The evidence registry has now independently rediscovered the same shape, which is either a good sign about the shape or a bad sign about the habit.
attrs.gap: Deliberately NOT implemented in R5.1. Migrating 51 records onto a product schema in the same round that repairs the consumption rule would make the repair unauditable.
attrs.statement: Evidence kind is not one dimension: logical force, origin, coverage, polarity and assurance are independent, and a flat enum can record only one of them at a time.
